ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Jim Thorpe — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Thorpe is a 63-year-old coach and speaker who comes for his yearly preventive visit two weeks after his last coronary disease review. His lip healed well after the excision three months ago. He has had no angina since the summer, has done 24 cardiac rehabilitation sessions, and now walks uphill to the ball field without stopping. The back strain settled within ten days. He smoked about a pack a day from his twenties until his heart attack eight years ago. He has never had colon cancer screening, lung cancer screening, or tests for HIV or hepatitis. He has thought about the information on Sac and Fox Nation and Indian Health Service programs and has decided to register with the urban Indian health program near his home for dental care, while keeping his medical care here. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1951-10-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 91.4 kg, BMI 26.7; blood pressure 122/76, pulse 60
Lip scar healed, soft and flat; mild actinic change of the upper lip only; mouth and tongue normal; no neck nodes
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no leg swelling
Soft and non-tender; no pulsatile mass
Sun-damaged skin of the face, neck and forearms; two rough scaly patches on the backs of the hands consistent with actinic keratoses; no suspicious pigmented lesions

Non-healing lesion of the left lower lip for about three months: a 1.2 cm firm, crusted ulcer on the vermilion that bleeds when touched, on a background of dry, scaly lips from years of outdoor work; no numbness of the lip or chin and no palpable neck nodes. Suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma; incisional biopsy taken today and otolaryngology consultation booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to his documented lip cancer; superseded by the biopsy diagnosis.

Chronic coronary disease with stable exertional angina: tightness in the chest when walking uphill or carrying loads for about a year, relieved by two or three minutes of rest, never at rest; heart attack eight years ago, treated in hospital, with no regular care or medicines since. Resting ECG: sinus rhythm with Q waves in the inferior leads. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heart attacks
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented heart disease.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lip (external vermilion): invasive, well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma on incisional biopsy; 1.2 cm, no palpable neck nodes; clinical stage T1 N0 (AJCC 8th edition, lip and oral cavity). Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented lip cancer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the cited sources do not record the type of his lip cancer.

Acute low back strain after lifting bags of infield clay while preparing a ball field: pain across the lower back without leg pain, numbness, weakness, or bladder or bowel change; no red flags apart from a recent, fully excised early lip cancer; resolved
S — Synthetic acute injury; not a historical claim.
Actinic keratoses: two rough, scaly patches on the backs of the hands, in sun-damaged skin; treated with cryotherapy
S — Synthetic finding at the preventive visit, consistent with the sun-exposure history.

list.item:
Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. He qualifies for yearly low-dose CT lung cancer screening (age 50 to 80, about 35 pack-years, quit within 15 years) and chose to start it after shared decision-making. He chose a stool immunochemical test for colorectal cancer screening. After discussion of benefits and harms he chose not to have a PSA test this year. [S]
Low-dose CT of the chest.
Stool immunochemical test kit given.
HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests today.
Influenza, PCV20 pneumococcal, and first recombinant zoster vaccines today; second zoster dose in two to six months.
Actinic keratoses on the hands to be treated with cryotherapy at the next visit.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Chronic coronary disease with stable angina (I25.119). No angina; blood pressure 122/76; LDL 51 mg/dL two weeks ago. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines given, as the coronary disease guideline advises. [S]
Continue current medicines and cardiac rehabilitation.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the left lower lip, excised (C00.1). No sign of recurrence or new lesion three months after excision. [S]
Lip, mouth and neck examination at the surveillance visit in three weeks.
Dental visit through the urban Indian health program, as he chose.

Guideline basis: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); Purchased/Referred Care (2026); Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Lung Cancer: Screening (2021); Colorectal Cancer: Screening (2021); Adult Immunization Schedule by Medical Condition and Other Indication (2026)

Follow-up: HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B results by phone; stool test result when returned; low-dose CT result at the next visit. Lip surveillance and coronary disease review in three weeks. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1951-10-26: four months after surgery: lip and neck surveillance, coronary disease review, and screening results. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. He said that if he were seriously ill he would want to be told plainly, to be treated near his family, and to have the chance to include the spiritual practices that matter to him, which he will describe himself when the time comes. He chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly. [S]
